FINDINGS 15.

The accused Ajuba, Munna Khan, Zarina and Bobby have been charged for the commission of offences punishable under sections 498- A/306/34 IPC.
16.

SECTION 306 IPC 306. Abetment of

SECTION 34 IPC "When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone".
17.
It is a settled law of criminal jurisprudence that a person is believed to be innocent till the guilt is proved against him.
This principle is called The Presumption of Innocence.
In another words, the accused is entitled to take advantage of reasonable doubt in respect of his crime.

Presumption of Innocence is a re-statement of the rule that in criminal matters the prosecution has the burden of proving guilt of the accused in order to be convicted of the crime of which he is charged.

18. In this backdrop, I proceed to delve upon the evidence adduced on behalf of the prosecution.
MATERIAL WITNESS 19.1
The prosecution has heavily relied upon the testimonies of PW1 Rabia, PW2 Mosin Khan, PW3 Zahid and PW5 Mannu Bibi.
PW1 is the mother of deceased, PW2 is the father of deceased, PW3 is the brother in law of deceased and PW5 is the grandmother of deceased.
19.2 PW1 Rabia, is complainant and happens to be mother of deceased.
She expressed her ignorance qua reason of death of her daughter.
However, in her statement recorded before SDM concerned, she had casted allegations of dowry death against the accused persons but in the court she has turned hostile qua these allegations.
She has been cross examined at length by Ld. Addl. PP for the State but she has not supported the prosecution's case on material aspects.

Similar is the deposition of PW2 Mosin Khan (father of deceased)
and PW3 Zahid (brother in law).
They have not deposed anything incriminating against the accused persons.
They were cross examined by Ld. Addl. PP for the State,
however, prosecution has failed to bring anything relevant against the accused persons.
19.4 It is nowhere stated by PW1, PW2 and PW3 whether deceased was beaten or tortured or harassed soon before her committing suicide.
Even, if it is believed that accused persons had beaten deceased then it is not proved by the prosecution that those beatings were related to the demand of dowry from the deceased.
It is also not proved that those beatings were given soon before her death.
PW1 and PW2 have admitted that deceased used to visit their house and used to tell that she was living with accused persons happily and she was having no problem at her in -law's house.
Therefore, it is clear that there was no instant incident or complaint of beating which occurred with the deceased soon before of her committing suicide.

19.5 Although, as per deposition of PW5 Mannu Bibi, PW1 informed her that deceased was beaten by her husband and in-laws but information given by PW1 Rabia to PW5 Mannu Bibi falls into the category of hearsay evidence which his not admissible against the accused persons.

Moreover, PW1 has not deposed even a single word against the accused persons and therefore, it is highly improbable that she had informed PW5 about the alleged tortured on the deceased at the hands of accused persons.
There is no MLC on record of the deceased with regard to those alleged beatings.

It is also admitted case that no police complaint was ever lodged against the accused persons qua those beatings and no photographs have been placed on record by the parents of the SC No. 735/2019, FIR No. 573/2019 Page No. 11 of 14 PS Bhalaswa Dairy State Vs. Ajuba & Ors.
deceased.

sentences.text: In absence of documentary evidence, allegations of beatings levelled by PW5 stand unproved and falls into the category of hearsay evidence.
An accused cannot be convicted on the basis of sweeping and vague allegations.

19.6 In S. S. Chheena Vs. Vijay Kumar Mahajan (2010) 12 SCC 190, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that abetment involves a mental process of instigating a person or intentionally aiding a person in doing of a thing.

entities.text: S. S. Chheena Vs. Vijay Kumar Mahajan (2010) 12 SCC 190
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Without a positive act on the part of the accused to instigate or aid in committing suicide, conviction cannot be sustained.

The intention of the legislature and ratio of the cases decided by the Supreme Court is clear that in order to convict a person under section 306 IPC there has to be a clear mens rea to commit the offence.

It also requires an active act or direct act which led the deceased to commit suicide seeing no option and that act must have been intended to push the deceased into such a position that he committed State vs Ajuba And Ors on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83144367/
7 suicide.
19.7

Applying the ratio of S. S. Chheena's case to the present set of facts, it is clear that prosecution has failed to prove any allegation against the accused persons in connection with suicide of the deceased.
The testimonies of PW1, PW2, PW3 and PW5 are absolutely silent in this respect as to how the conduct of the accused persons instigated or aided the suicide of the deceased.
PRESUMPTION UNDER SECTION 113A OF INDIAN EVIDENCE ACT 20.1
The law has undergone radical changes due to insertion of section 113A of the Evidence Act.

Under the said section, if a bride commit suicide within 7 years of marriage, and if there is evidence of ill treatment by the husband or other members of the in-laws family, the burden shifts onto the SC No. 735/2019, FIR No. 573/2019 Page No. 12 of 14 PS Bhalaswa Dairy State Vs. Ajuba & Ors.
accused husband or such other members figuring as accused to show that there was no abetment.

entities.text: PS Bhalaswa Dairy State Vs. Ajuba & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The presumption under section 113A of Evidence Act, is applicable in the present case as the marriage was solemnized four months back to her death and the deceased committed suicide on 05.09.2019.
But to shift the burden upon the accused persons, prosecution was duty bound to prove the fact that deceased was subjected to cruelty by the husband and other members of his family.

As stated above, prosecution has failed to extract anything out of PW1, PW2, PW3 and PW5 against the accused persons to shift the burden upon the accused persons under section 113A of Indian Evidence Act.
Therefore, this court is of the considered view that prosecution has failed to prove the allegations under section 306 IPC against the accused persons for want of cogent and reliable evidence.
20.2 As far as allegations under section 498A IPC are concerned, there is no evidence at all that deceased was subjected to cruelty by the accused persons in connection with their demand of dowry.

In Rajrani Vs. State (Delhi Administration) (2000) 10 SCC 662, the Supreme Court held that while considering the case of cruelty in the context of the provision of section 498-A IPC, the court must examine that allegations/acquisition must be of very grave nature and should be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
20.3 The basic ingredient of section 498-A IPC is that a married woman was subjected to cruelty to meet unlawful demand of property or valuable security.

As discussed above the depositions of material witnesses PW1, PW2, PW3 and PW5 are silent with regard to any cruelty done with the deceased by the accused persons to meet any unlawful demand of property or valuable security.
Hence, case of the prosecution qua allegation under section SC No. 735/2019, FIR No. 573/2019 Page No. 13 of 14 PS Bhalaswa Dairy State Vs. Ajuba & Ors.

Thus, in view of the aforesaid findings, since there are material contradictions and improvisations in the testimony of material witnesses, there is no hesitation in holding that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubts and accordingly the accused Ajuba, Munna Khan, Zarina and Bobby stand acquitted of the charges levelled against them.
